newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Spain leaves key rate steady.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Spain leaves key rate steady.

text.p: Following are comments from economists after the Bank of Spain left its key money market rate unchanged on Tuesday at 5.25 percent.

On Friday, a Reuter poll showed mixed forecasts on a possible cut, with some analysts saying that the central bank had the scope for further easing but that the economy was not suggesting an immediate move.
JUAN ANTONIO MIELGO, ECONOMIST AT BANK OF AMERICA IN MADRID

"To me we have to wait until the next repo auction on July 3, where current expections would be shifted. There is scope. It seems to me this is a cautious attitude of the Bank of Spain and as the markets had not priced in any cut the decision to wait could even be taken as a positive one".
ALFREDO URRUTIA, ECONOMIST AT SOCIETE GENERALE IN MADRID

"I am personally surprised and I thought it was going to cut. Also a good part of the market expected that as can be seen by the high volume of bids unallotted. (Over 3.38 trillion pesetas bids the central bank allotted 1.527 trillion pesetas)".
"Maybe the Bank of Spain wanted to send a message to stop enthusiasm and is trying to hold in the most aggressive expectations..but the scope for further cuts is still there".
CARMEN HERNANSANZ, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH IN MADRID

"I think that until the market prices in another rate cut, the Bank of Spain will hold its key rate. Expectations of another cut would be transferred to another repo, beacuse the scope is still there".
ELENA PAGOLA, ECONOMIST AT AFI IN MADRID

"In my opinion, the Bank of Spain opted for a cautious stance until it could verify the expected pick-up in CPI would really be in line with expectations and until the national statistic institute INE would not announce the quarterly data on economic growth (first quarter GDP is scheduled tomorrow)".
